mechanism_narrative: The ongoing recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT from t-2w to t-0w will lift discretionary stopovers and lunch-time shopping, so RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks relative to the last four weeks.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue improving but mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than the prior 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays above 38 percent for several weeks, more time spent near home shifts spending to neighborhood retail, so RETAIL_REC edges up within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains at or above 38 for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains elevated for two weeks but RETAIL_REC does not increase within the following two weeks, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A synchronized drop in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES of at least five points week-on-week signals renewed suppression of movement and in-person commerce, which pushes RETAIL_REC down over the next week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall by 5+ points week-on-week
failure_condition: If both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES drop sharply but RETAIL_REC does not decline in the following week, this mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS mobility first diverts discretionary outings away from malls and restaurants, so retail activity remains weak for up to four weeks after PARKS rises.
failure_condition: If PARKS rises but RETAIL_REC is flat or higher over the next four weeks, the hypothesis is false.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM holds near its current level while RESIDENTIAL falls from the high-30s, household errand consolidation weakens and more trips spill into retail venues, lifting RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 39 while GROCERY_PHARM does not decline
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL drops below 39 without a later rise in RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A short-horizon stabilization in PARKS and TRANSIT after prior declines indicates normalization of outdoor and travel routines, which should lift retail footfall within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS and TRANSIT stop falling for 1 week after a decline
failure_condition: If PARKS and TRANSIT stabilize but RETAIL_REC does not increase within two weeks, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: As WORKPLACES approaches its current trough and then turns up, commuting-linked purchases and after-work shopping should improve, so RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises after at least two consecutive weekly declines
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES turns upward but RETAIL_REC remains below its prior four-week mean over the next month, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT keeps recovering while RESIDENTIAL eases down from above 40, the balance shifts from staying home to going out, creating a near-term increase in retail and recreation mobility within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises and RESIDENTIAL falls in the same week
failure_condition: If TRANSIT rises while RESIDENTIAL falls but RETAIL_REC does not increase in the following week, the hypothesis fails.
